title: Adaptive signal throttling and pager sensitivity tune after capacity-driven SLO incidents
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity degradation event on 2026-02-28 we observed multiple SLO breach alerts and high pager churn caused by a combination of conservative burn-rate thresholds, lack of tier-aware paging, and redundant signals from both latency and token-queue metrics. This ticket coordinates the follow-up work to reduce noisy page storms while preserving rapid detection of real customer-impacting degradations. Goals: 1) reduce actionable pager volume by ~60% for tiered services, 2) ensure burn-rate alerts remain sensitive to fast regressions, 3) add tooling to simulate alert load before rolling changes, and 4) update runbooks and oncall playbooks with the new behavior and escalation paths.
action_items: Marco Ruiz - Implement tier-aware paging rules: map burn-rate windows and paging thresholds to customer tier metadata; 5 days; due 2026-03-20
Lena Cho - Add dedupe layer in alerting pipeline to collapse concurrent signals from latency and queue-depth into a single incident with aggregated context; 3 days; due 2026-03-18
Devon Hart - Add synthetic load tests that exercise burn-rate alerts and page suppression to staging and run through chaos scenarios; 4 days; due 2026-03-22
Asha Patel - Re-tune burn-rate windows: add short (1m), medium (5m), and sustained (30m) tiers and document expected sensitivity trade-offs; 2 days; due 2026-03-12
SRE Team - Create rollback-safe feature flag for new alert thresholds and run a 2-week dark launch on internal services; 3 days coordination; due 2026-03-25
Infra - Instrument queue_wait_time SLI for request routing to improve signal fidelity; 6 days; due 2026-03-26
Observability - Add a dashboard that visualizes correlated burn-rate, token_throughput, and queue_wait_time by region and customer tier; 4 days; due 2026-03-21
Oncall - Update runbook with new paging escalation matrix and include examples of false-positive signatures (maintenance, autoscaling ramp); 1 day; due 2026-03-15
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume for infra SLO alerts reduced by at least 50% in the first 7 days after rollout (measured against baseline 2026-02-20 to 2026-02-28)
Burn-rate alerts still trigger for fast regressions: validated by synthetic test that introduces a 40% error-rate spike within 2 minutes
New dedupe layer collapses multi-signal incidents into one ticket with combined context in >=90% of simulated overlap cases
Runbook updated and oncall team trained; a short tabletop exercise completed with at least 2 oncall rotations
All changes are behind feature flags with automated rollback and a clear metric-driven rollback policy
updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after incident review (incident ID INC-2026-02-28-07). Initial triage identified three root contributors: aggressive burn-rate sensitivity, lack of tier differentiation for paging, and duplicate alert signals.

2026-03-07: Design review with SRE and Observability teams. Decision: introduce a dedupe layer and tier-aware paging rather than raising global thresholds to keep sensitivity for high-priority customers.
2026-03-09: Prototype dedupe logic implemented in alert-transformer service; initial tests show 70% reduction in duplicate alerts in local test harness (see link to PR)
2026-03-11: Shortlisting burn-rate windows and their expected P99 reaction times (1m, 5m, 30m). Agreed to keep short window for automated rollback triggers and medium window for paging decisions.
2026-03-12: Asha pushed the burn-rate tuning doc to Confluence (link). Next: staging rollout under feature flag.
2026-03-14: Marco started implementation of tier-aware paging rules. Observability began building the combined dashboard. Scheduled tabletop exercise for 2026-03-17.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: raising global thresholds reduces noise but increases time-to-detect for regressions. The chosen approach prioritizes preservation of short-window sensitivity while preventing paging for transient, low-impact noise.
We decided against removing burn-rate alerts completely for lower tiers; instead implement a delayed paging policy (notify-no-page) for P3 customers and immediate page for P0/P1.
This work will inform a broader alert hygiene initiative planned for Q2 that will include automated alert ownership and lifecycle rules.
